test a simple median over the full pool to see if a robust non-weighted combiner beats the weighted pool4 baseline in this trend-dominated, low-seasonality series.
try a weighted combination on the full pool using inverse_error to see if full‑pool weighting beats the limited pool.

trend_dominated and moderate ranking suggest a simple mean might capture the shared trend without overfitting to noise, testing a different combination type (mean).
test a per‑horizon top‑k mean weighting on the full pool (w5) to see if horizon‑specific diversity helps trend‑dominated series.
trend dominated, high predictability, and moderate ranking stability suggest a robust, simple aggregation like median over the stable pool4 may perform well without overfitting.
test a trimmed‑mean on the stable 6‑model pool (trend‑dominated, moderate ranking stability) to see if removing the two worst models improves the weighted blend.
Test a simple mean combination on the stable 6‑model pool to see if uniform averaging beats the weighted softmax, given the strong trend dominance and moderate ranking stability.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.068. Series context: trend strength 0.9694 and seasonal strength 0.0007; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.485); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 89.831.
